hypothesis: The previous fused candidate was correct and measured 0.459449 ms with up to 8192 partials. Keeping its approximate 4096-elements-per-partial policy but raising the cap to 16384 halves the large-input chunk size and doubles finalizer fan-in at the largest size. This tests whether more first-stage CTAs improve large-input parallelism enough to offset the more expensive finalizer; no speedup is assumed.
notes: One bounded contrast: preserve contiguous scalar loads, CUB per-CTA reduction, and the 4096 target while increasing the partial-count cap and thus the maximum finalizer fan-in. Every launched first-stage CTA writes its partial, and the finalizer overwrites output. The controller must validate correctness and measure full-call time.
transformations: Replace the two full-size absolute-value and atomic-sum passes with a fused first-stage sum(abs(x)) and one partial write per CTA.
Retain approximately 4096 input elements per partial, but raise the maximum partial count from 8192 to 16384; each CTA covers a contiguous input chunk with scalar loads.
Use a single 256-thread CUB finalizer to reduce all current-call partials and overwrite output; zero-length input explicitly overwrites output with zero.
